beats.say: Hubble has watched the universe since 1990. Now it is slowly falling, and NASA is asking companies how to save it.
Hubble orbits in low Earth orbit. Up there the air is incredibly thin, but it is not zero.
Every lap, Hubble brushes through that thin air. The drag steals a little speed, so it sinks a little lower.
Lower down, the air gets thicker. So the drag grows, and the fall speeds up.
Hubble has no engine to push itself back up. Astronauts used to boost it, but the space shuttle retired in 2011.
NASA's analysis says Hubble could fall back into the atmosphere around 2033 or 2034.
So NASA asked industry for ideas. Option one: boost it to a higher orbit, and buy more years of science.
Option two: service it, and upgrade it. Option three: bring it down safely, in a controlled re-entry.
Any mission would need to fly by 2032. Companies have until November thirtieth to reply.
